clue.text: Hesitate in front of hero, former champion

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: former, as in old times, is old
to champion a cause is to back it

explanation.surface: An athlete holds back from facing a hero who once held the title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' reads as a noun beside 'former', but it is the verb meaning to support.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back is to refrain or be reluctant, which is a synonym of hesitating.

clue.text: Agitated man set to climb

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letters run upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: Someone is nervous about a man getting ready to scale a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, climbing means the word reads upwards. Het up is mainly British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Het up is an informal adjective for anxious or excited, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Party member's unsparing protest about traitor

blocks.note: liberal means generous, giving freely without stint
a demo is a short word for a protest march
c is short for circa, about
a rat is a betrayer or turncoat

explanation.surface: A politician makes a relentless protest about someone who has betrayed the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a link to the traitor, but it is C, short for circa. The Liberal Democrats are a UK political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liberal Democrat belongs to Britain's Liberal Democrat party, so is an example of a party member.

clue.text: Nonsense about fair and legendary creature? You'll find volumes on it

indicators.note: one word placed about another surrounds it on both sides

blocks.note: bosh is a dated word for rubbish or nonsense
an elf is a creature of folklore

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a fairy tale and points to where the books can be found.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: volumes are books, which sit on this piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Books, also called volumes, stand on a shelf built for them, so this cryptic hint describes the furniture.

clue.text: Low point reached by school expelling odd characters

indicators.note: throwing out the first, third and fifth letters leaves only the even-placed ones

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of school

explanation.surface: A school sinks to a new low after expelling its strange pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd characters' looks like eccentric people, but means the letters in odd positions.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is the lowest point of a ridge between two peaks, a mountain pass.

clue.text: Saloon for instance with favourite floor covering

blocks.note: a saloon is a type of car (a sedan in the US)
a teacher's pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A saloon bar is decorated with its favourite rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' suggests a bar, but in Britain a saloon is a car body style.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpet is a woven textile laid across a floor, so it covers the floor.

clue.text: Some diplomats easily baffled

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a part of their letters is used

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A few diplomats are readily confused.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at sea is an idiom for being confused or bewildered.

clue.text: Hasn't fate dealt badly with people in this film?

indicators.note: something badly dealt with is mishandled, so these letters get mixed up

explanation.surface: A question about whether destiny treated humanity harshly in some movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is split: 'dealt badly with' sits between the two parts. The surface fits the film, where humans are ruled by apes.
explanation.definitionFit: Planet of the Apes is a 1968 science-fiction movie, so it is an example of a film.

clue.text: Thinker's article on wild riots

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the next word's letters run loose

explanation.surface: An intellectual writes a piece about violent unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece, but it is the word 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorist works out ideas and principles, so is someone who thinks for a living.

clue.text: Volunteers express contempt for ban

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers jeer at a prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo is a social or religious prohibition, so it serves as a noun synonym.

clue.text: Pass laws with support I condemn

blocks.note: to slate is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: A lawmaker passes legislation backed by the support they deplore.
explanation.walkthrough: To slate is British slang for criticising severely.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make laws, which Parliament does by passing them.

clue.text: Aged drunk bothered noble ruler

indicators.note: bothered means flustered, so the preceding letters are thrown into disarray

explanation.surface: An elderly inebriate pesters an aristocratic monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand duke rules a grand duchy such as Luxembourg, a noble of sovereign rank.

clue.text: Old man, artist with very large sunshade

blocks.note: pa is a father, an old man in slang
so, as in so good, means very

explanation.surface: A father and a painter shelter under an enormous parasol.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a light umbrella carried or set up to give shade from the sun.

clue.text: Walk after meal round a point of departure

indicators.note: a thing placed round another encloses it
coming after means written later, so one piece follows the other

blocks.note: to pad is to walk softly

explanation.surface: Someone takes a stroll after eating, circling a starting place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point of departure' sounds abstract, but it is the literal place a rocket leaves from.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch pad is the platform rockets leave from, and figuratively any springboard for a venture.

clue.text: Partner in mood endlessly unprofessional

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
without an end means the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: an aura is a feeling or atmosphere

explanation.surface: A spouse is in a bad mood and acting unprofessionally.
explanation.walkthrough: AURA loses its last letter to AUR, which then holds MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur does something without being paid, so is not a professional.

clue.text: Unhappy with material, so she played an Elvis classic

indicators.note: played as in toyed with, so the letters are messed about

explanation.surface: A sad woman, fed up with fabric, put on a famous Presley record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played' seems to mean she performed the song, but it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue Suede Shoes is a 1956 rock and roll hit recorded by Elvis Presley.

clue.text: Love put into opening tune, English gem set alone

indicators.note: something put into another goes inside it

blocks.note: a slit is a narrow opening
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A romantic song is played at the start, an English jewel standing apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening tune' reads as an overture, but opening and tune are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitaire is a single diamond or other stone mounted on its own in a ring.

clue.text: Psychic power in strange final period of existence

indicators.note: strange means odd or unusual, so the word that follows is rearranged
placed in something means set inside it

explanation.surface: A medium senses something odd about the last stage of life.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of final split around ESP.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifespan is the length of time a creature lives, the duration of its existence.

clue.text: One with fee cut, faintly troubled, showing weakness

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters before it are stirred up

explanation.surface: Someone whose pay was reduced is mildly upset and looks feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineffectuality is the quality of failing to have any effect, a kind of feebleness.

clue.text: Alliance finally became split in vanity project

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: as in got angry, became angry
a rip is a tear or split

explanation.surface: A coalition eventually broke apart over a self-indulgent scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like the alliance breaking up, but it is a noun meaning a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity undertaken mainly to boost one's own self-importance.

clue.text: Provoke arguments in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means as it reaches the ear, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: rows, rhyming with cows, are quarrels

explanation.surface: Stirring up quarrels at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' suggests a court case; here it marks a sound-alike. A row (rhymes with cow) is British for a noisy quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse someone is to stir them up or provoke them to action or anger.

clue.text: In context remembrance is intense

indicators.note: in means found inside, so the letters lie within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Remembering something in its setting can be a powerful experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme describes something very great in degree, the same sense as intense.

clue.text: Country for example with unknown part

explanation.surface: A nation, say, with a region nobody has explored.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a nation in North Africa, so it is an instance of a country.

clue.text: New drapes due to be brought round

indicators.note: a new version of these words means their letters are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: Fresh curtains are expected to be delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought round' sounds like a delivery, but it means won over.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone round is an idiom for convincing them to change their view.

clue.text: Pair united in act

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word that follows

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: Two performers working together on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a set of two people, especially musicians or performers, so it is a couple.

clue.text: Merely dropping small hint

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it fall away, so a letter goes

blocks.note: simply, as in simply a joke, means merely
the clothing size abbreviation, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Just letting slip a tiny clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply is to suggest something indirectly, which is what hinting does.

clue.text: Talk reflected on temperature and effect of sun

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front

blocks.note: re means on the subject of

explanation.surface: A chat looking back on the heat and what sunshine does to skin.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, T and TAN together are written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Natter is a British informal word for chatting idly, so a synonym of talk.

clue.text: Area containing Glastonbury Tor seems changed

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters before it take a new order

explanation.surface: The landscape around the famous hill near Glastonbury looks different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glastonbury Tor' reads as one name, but the definition stops at Glastonbury and Tor starts the fodder. Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is the English county where the town of Glastonbury lies, so it is the region that includes it.
